title: Outlook for Mac: Purview Data Loss Prevention for calendar events
summary: Hold: the PowerShell example invites administrators to supply mailboxes to a parameter whose documented valid value is All. The briefing also asserts that particular DLP actions can stop calendar invites without documentation confirming that behaviour for this feature.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The cited page documents Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy, for another location type as the note explains.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Go to Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -ExchangeLocation <mailboxes> -Mode <PolicyMode> selects the mailboxes covered by a DLP policy and its mode.
claims.quote: The ExchangeLocation parameter specifies whether to include email messages in the DLP policy. The valid value for this parameter is All.
claims.fix: Replace the call in the front matter and rendered table with 'New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -ExchangeLocation All -Mode <PolicyMode>'. Add to the row note: 'This call includes email for all users; -ExchangeLocation does not accept a mailbox list.'

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy runs in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents DLP policy tips for email in Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS now supports data loss prevention (DLP) policy tips with commonly used predicates and exceptions, advanced classifiers, and override capabilities.
claims.fix: After the email-support statement, add: 'Microsoft's troubleshooting article still says policy tips are not supported for Outlook for Mac iOS clients, conflicting with this platform-specific reference (https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/microsoft-365/data-loss-prevention/data-loss-prevention-policy-tips#client-doesn%27t-support-mailtips).' Keep the platform-specific reference as the source for the documented email control.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: General DLP guidance documents Block with override and Block actions.
claims.quote: Block with override: The user activity is blocked by default. You can audit the event, raise alerts and notifications.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: If a rule uses Block with override or Block, users can be stopped from sending a calendar invite.
claims.quote: Searched: "Outlook" "calendar" "DLP" "policy tips" default permissions alerts Activity explorer. Read dlp-create-deploy-policy and the mobile/macOS and Outlook for Microsoft 365 references; none confirms these actions for this planned calendar capability.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence beginning 'If a rule uses Block with override or Block' with: 'Learn documents Block with override and Block as general DLP actions; Microsoft has not yet documented which actions apply to calendar events in Outlook for Mac.'

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: General DLP deployment states include simulation, simulation with policy tips, full enforcement and off.
claims.quote: Run the policy in simulation mode; Run the policy in simulation mode and show policy tips while in simulation mode; Turn it on right away; Keep it off

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft's general deployment guidance recommends simulation with policy tips scoped to a pilot before full enforcement.
claims.quote: When you change the state to Run the policy in simulation mode and show policy tips, narrow your scope to a pilot group that can give you feedback and be early adopters who can be a resource for others when they come onboard.
